div.div: The Problem: A 3-node Kafka cluster in 3 different AZs replicates every message 3 times. If you ingest 100TB of data, that data crosses AZ boundaries twice (once to each replica). At scale, your "networking" bill can actually become higher than your "compute" bill.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(#ffffff, var(--ge-dark-color, #121212)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 508px; height: 1px; padding-top: 155px; margin-left: 281px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
The Fix:
1. Compression: Use Zstd or Snappy to shrink the data before it leaves the node.
2. Rack Awareness: Configure Kafka/Cassandra with "Rack Awareness" so clients try to read from a replica in their own AZ (free) rather than reaching across to another AZ (paid).
